goal: Establish one honest asset-indexed catalogue, perfect the solve-x shell, stop for human desktop approval, and only after approval host all concrete assets and derive a human-reviewed canonical port queue.

slices.title: Freeze catalogue source inventory
slices.summary: Frozen the pre-change catalogue source map. The baseline distinguishes 33 concrete assets and 10 lazy packs from 50 descriptors, 34 Workbench identities, 41 display rows, 69 Workbench relationships, and 82 display representations. It records concrete identity/loading, mixed projection, adapter, route, and review-capture ownership; preserves all existing routes; and fixes the next boundary at one row per concrete loadable ID without changing runtime or visual behavior. Focused 21/21, full 3130/3130, typecheck, build, promotion memory, diff hygiene, and workspace validation pass.

slices.title: Characterize loadable asset registry
slices.summary: Added a compact typed loadable registry that groups the generated editor metadata by concrete animation ID, requires one exact asset-level descriptor, records one lazy pack owner, and carries no renderer, representation, lifecycle, or roadmap state. Characterization proves one entry for each of the 33 concrete assets, successful resolution across all 10 packs, and exclusion of seven reader-only playable display IDs plus the planned quadratic identity. Eight focused tests, full typecheck, architecture, diff hygiene, and workspace validation pass; no runtime consumer or visual behavior changed.

slices.title: Separate concrete from planned identities
slices.summary: Catalogue membership now equals the 33 lazy-loadable concrete identities exactly; the one planned quadratic identity remains immutable context outside catalogue rows, and projection drift fails closed without mutating caller-owned records.

slices.title: Map surface adapter hostability
slices.summary: Added a read-only hostability seam that distinguishes target dispatch from actual adapter resolution. The current 33-asset map is 31 ready, 2 missing-adapter, and 0 unsupported-surface: programming.add and the synchronized equation/programming comparison lack a programming adapter. Generic and specialized priority ownership remains intact; no renderer, loader, runtime, or visual behavior changed.

slices.title: Map related context sprawl
slices.summary: Frozen the related-context map: 33 concrete assets currently fan out to 50 descriptors, 69 Workbench relationships, and 74 concrete display contexts (52 editor, 17 card, 3 reader, 2 diagnostic). Solve-x is widest at seven contexts. Seven reader-only playable display IDs remain preserved route evidence but cannot mint catalogue rows. Generated display metadata is the runtime context source; source-rich Workbench control, review, roadmap, and promotion state stays outside catalogue membership.

slices.title: Build asset-first catalogue projection
slices.summary: Built the lightweight asset-first projection: each loadable registry member receives primary metadata, pack identity, explicit domains/families/samples, honest tags, separate fuzzy-search terms, and exact-ID related contexts. Planned and display-only playable identities cannot enter. The runtime projection imports generated metadata only and carries no Workbench, project-control, promotion, hostability, adapter, renderer, or asset-pack implementation state.

slices.title: Prove one row per concrete asset
slices.summary: Proved the catalogue cardinality law: 33 unique projected row IDs exactly equal the 33 loadable registry IDs and the 33 assets resolved from their exact packs. The 50 descriptors and 74 globally unique related contexts remain subordinate metadata, and duplicate loadable membership fails before a row can render.

slices.title: Derive honest catalogue health
slices.summary: Derived honest catalogue health from adapter hostability, observed paint, diagnostics, and explicit review need: the pre-host baseline is 0 Ready, 31 Review, and 2 Broken, independent from promotion and reviewer disposition.

slices.title: Add stable catalogue visual command
slices.summary: Added stable npm run visual:animation-catalogue backed by a repo-owned Chromium capture script. It records the current solve-x Workbench bootstrap at the desktop review viewport to disposable tmp/codex output, providing an inspected before-state that later shell slices can tighten without changing the command.

slices.title: Establish default catalogue route
slices.summary: Made the asset catalogue the canonical empty-query route with an explicit animation-catalogue alias. The editor, Workbench, library host, and tutorial remain preserved explicit views; returning to the editor now writes view=editor rather than colliding with the new default. The temporary catalogue render is intentionally minimal and contains no old dashboard machinery.

slices.title: Bind solve-x exemplar selection
slices.summary: Bound the default and explicit artifact route to the exact solve-x catalogue entry, primary descriptor, and algebra lazy asset pack. Known sibling assets remain typed deferred states until exemplar approval, and unknown IDs render not-found evidence instead of silently falling back. The explicit deep link now restores an observable selected state.

slices.title: Build three-region desktop shell
slices.summary: Built the solve-x desktop shell as exactly three full-height sibling regions: a compact flat asset rail with derived Review health, a frameless center stage host, and one linear Details inspector. It has no masthead, iframe, nested navigation, ontology tree, cards, representation picker, or sibling hosting. The stage remains a deliberate placeholder until s13 binds the preserved player.

slices.title: Make center stage frameless and persistent
slices.summary: Mounted the established solve-x player and equation adapter directly inside the fixed center region with the existing listener/hydration order and deterministic initial state. Catalogue stage chrome is removed and the stage remains visible without page scrolling. The inherited settings still visible below the stage are intentionally left for the immediately following transport-reduction slice.

slices.title: Reduce universal controls to transport
slices.summary: Added an opt-in compact catalogue projection of the established player: the default surface now renders only Play/Pause and the scrubber with percentage. Extra transport buttons, settings, diagnostics, and authoring chrome remain available in the unchanged full editor projection, while the focusable player's Space, arrow, Home/End, and R keyboard laws and deterministic runtime remain intact.

slices.title: Apply inline math and compact heading scale
slices.summary: Made inline KaTeX an explicit catalogue-player layout request consumed by the established equation adapter; the full editor remains display-mode by default. Layout participates in replaceable content identity but not stable stage or runtime identity. The shell keeps one clipped semantic h1, no visible h1/h2, and h3-scale visible Details typography.

slices.title: Add flat fuzzy search rail
slices.summary: Added a single flat fuzzy search rail over all 33 concrete assets. Filtering replaces only the inventory list, keeps solve-x mounted, and marks unobserved siblings Review pending post-checkpoint hosting.

slices.title: Dock compact review capture lower left
slices.summary: Docked a compact development-only Review box in the lower-left rail and reused the established capture pipeline for solve-x artifact identity, playhead, render ownership, viewport, and build state. The open capture path is live-verified and production-erased. The existing protocol has no bitmap screenshot field, so screenshot attachment is recorded as an explicit remaining evidence gap rather than falsely claimed.

slices.title: Add linear Details inspector
slices.summary: Expanded the one right-hand Details inspector into a stable linear projection: identity, semantics, playback, capabilities, health evidence, and related contexts. Empty sections disappear; there are no tabs, cards, buttons, or nested navigation. Preserved editor-context links now explicitly name view=editor after the catalogue became the default route.

slices.title: Separate parameters from review tuning
slices.summary: Added one compact inspector selector that shows Details, Parameters, or Tuning one at a time. Solve-x honestly has no exposed semantic Parameters. Tuning contains only the existing Style and Focus review controls, routed through the established player authority without remount or duplicate clock. Review capture now carries bounded parameter/tuning evidence maps; no universal artifact control schema was introduced.

slices.title: Preserve URL keyboard and accessibility state
slices.summary: Added bounded shareable playhead state to the catalogue route and initialized the preserved player directly from it. Runtime frame events canonically replace the URL without adding history entries; zero stays clean. Search, inspector mode, and tuning remain transient. Live checks prove Space, Arrow, Home, End, and system reduced-motion behavior through the simplified host without extra default chrome.

slices.title: Prove solve-x preservation boundary
slices.summary: Proved the solve-x catalogue is a host projection over the established lazy algebra asset, primary descriptor, player/runtime clock, dense reverse law, equation dispatch, and native KaTeX adapter. A focused executable boundary compares forward and rewind frames directly and forbids catalogue ownership of runtime, renderer, asset-pack, or solve-x implementation imports. Focused 45/45, live Chromium, typecheck, architecture, and production-review closure pass.

slices.title: Capture desktop solve-x exemplar
slices.summary: Captured and inspected the solve-x desktop exemplar at the stable 1440 by 1000 review viewport. Durable criteria freeze three flat regions, one fuzzy rail, persistent frameless stage, compact transport, inline KaTeX, one inspector mode, compact headings, and lower-left Review. The disposable bitmap remains evidence rather than a golden, and promotion remains shell-only.
